items.title: Godfrey Hirsch Interview, 1987-11-10
items.q: I did the Colgate Hour with Peggy Lee

ctx.x: I was the founder of the Festival of Flowers, which is an annual affair that they still have going on. Then I wrote the Sugar Bowl Parade and then I was at the Sanger Theatre. I was 24 years old and I did that and played the first notes for the first time on several, on two New Orleans TV stations. WDSU, when they went NBC, I was the first note to hit it on a timpani and the first note to hit a chime on WWL when they went on the air. As the president of a National Rental Association, I was probably not for two…
What did he do? He was the son of. The son of the conductor of that. I can't think of his name right now.
